newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Bank Menatep to issue ADR by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Russia Bank Menatep to issue ADR by year-end.

text.p: Bank Menatep, Russia's 11th biggest bank by assets, said on Monday it will issue level-one American Depositary Receipts by the end of 1996 following central bank permission to sell its shares to foreigners.
Menatep said in a statement ADRs could cover up to three percent of the bank's shares, comprising 1.5 million preferred shares and 1.5 million ordinary shares.
The shares have a dual face value of $1 and 1,000 roubles even though that does not correspond to the exchange rate.
Russian bank shares are rarely traded in Russia and are highly illiquid.

Menatep received permission from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to issue ADRs in June, but the paper was not traded, as Russian legislation requires central bank approval for each deal in banks' shares with foreigners.
One ADR will cover 10 shares, Menatep said. The bank's authorised capital is 100 billion roubles.
Bank of New York is Menatep's depositary and ING-Eurasia is its custodian.
Inkombank and Bank Vozrozhdeniye have also received SEC permission to issue ADRs, and Inkombank received central bank permission to sell its paper to foreigners last week.
